children: The Indian stock market will remain closed on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, on account of Guru Nanak Jayanti. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) will suspend trading across their equity and derivatives segments for the day. According to the exchanges' holiday calendars for 2026, trading in the equity market and equity derivatives segment will remain closed on Tuesday. The Nifty 50 and Sensex will not trade during the session.
The exchanges will resume normal trading on Wednesday, November 25, with the regular market session running from 9:15 am to 3:30 pm.
Will MCX remain closed on November 24?
The Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will remain closed during the morning session on Tuesday, November 24, but trading will resume in the evening.
According to MCX's trading schedule, the morning session runs from 9 am to 5 pm, while the evening session begins at 5 pm and continues until 11:30 pm or 11:55 pm, depending on the contract.
Trading in eligible commodity contracts, including gold, silver and crude oil futures, will be available during the evening session.
When will stock market trading resume?
Trading on the NSE and BSE will resume on Wednesday, November 25, 2026.
The regular equity market session will open at 9:15 am and close at 3:30 pm. The pre-open session will begin at 9 am.
The holiday leaves investors with four trading sessions during the week: Monday, November 23; Wednesday, November 25; Thursday, November 26; and Friday, November 27.

November 24 is also a settlement holiday. Certain credits arising from trades executed on the previous trading day may not be reflected in investors' trading account balances on the holiday. Regular withdrawal requests may also be processed according to the revised settlement schedule.
Investors should check their broker's settlement and withdrawal timelines to understand how the holiday may affect their funds.
When is the next stock market holiday?
The next scheduled trading holiday after Guru Nanak Jayanti will be Christmas on Friday, December 25, 2026.

title: Stock market holiday November 24: NSE, BSE to remain closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti
